summary.text: Robbyn Lewis is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 46 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She is on the November ballot with fellow incumbents Luke Clippinger and Mark Edelson and Jeremy Amason for the district's three seats.
Her background is in public health, and she serves on the Environment and Transportation Committee.

paragraphs.text: Robbyn Lewis was born in Gary, Indiana, and graduated from the Latin School of Chicago in 1981.
She earned a B.A. in anthropology from the University of Chicago in 1990 and an M.P.H. in international health from Columbia University in 1998.
Lewis was a Peace Corps volunteer in Niger from 1990 to 1991, according to her legislative biography.

She later worked in public health, including as a program manager at Jhpiego from 1999 to 2006, regional manager for West and South Africa at Ipas from 2012 to 2014, and special assistant at the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange from 2014 to 2017.
The biography lists her as a civic data and engagement fellow with the University of Baltimore and Baltimore Neighborhood Indicators Alliance beginning in 2019.
Lewis assumed office on January 10, 2017, according to Ballotpedia.
The General Assembly website lists her as a member of the Environment and Transportation Committee.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Lewis described herself as a leader in health care, transit, and safe and livable communities and as the first African American woman to represent District 46.

She listed her three key campaign messages as affordability, accountability and opportunity, and named public health, transportation, housing and livable communities, small business and economic development as policy areas she is passionate about.
